recipes.name: Slow Cooker Lime Cilantro Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.25 ounce) package dry taco seasoning mix
3 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Stir salsa, taco seasoning, lime juice, and cilantro together in a slow cooker until well combined. Add chicken and spoon salsa mixture over top to coat.

Cover and cook until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, on Low for 6 to 8 hours or High for 4 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Shred chicken in the crock with two forks, then mix with the sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Lime Cilantro Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker lime cilantro chicken is so easy with just five ingredients. Load some up on a hard or soft tortillas for some truly tasty tacos.

video.description: A tender, tasty taco filling, chicken cooks low and slow in a simple Mexican-inspired salsa.

review.reviewBody: I used a good quality salsa, double-batch of homemade taco seasoning and double the cilantro. I made the end result into fajitas with sauteed red pepper, sweet onion and minced garlic. As always, I think the quality of your ingredients can make or break your recipe--I'm glad I doubled the spices and used a good salsa. We were quite hungry today so this fed us well with enough leftover for another meal, with the sauteed vegetables. I'll make this again.

This was one of the easiest and tastiest slow cooker recipes I have come across so far! I had chicken in the freezer, had bought fresh cilantro for another recipe and barely used any of it, had a lime on hand and had just whipped up some Taco Seasoning II (from this website). Plus I always have spare jars of salsa on hand. I used it as taco/burrito filling. Whole wheat tortillas with some shredded cheese and taco seasoned rice...delicious!

I used 2.5 lb boneless chicken breast and did not put the liquid ingredients in to cook. Crock pot on high for 1.5 hours was completely cooked.I used Tajin seasoning ( has citrus flavor with a special chili powder and salt) garlic powder, black pepper and fresh cilantro instead of salt and taco seasoning. I put 1/2 chopped onion in bottom of crock pot before adding 1/2 thawed chicken breast cut into smaller pieces and it cooked in 1.5 hours it it's own juices. ( I have found it is better and cooks faster not to add any liquid to crock pot when cooking chicken) I had a portion as it was and very good. Then after it was cooked I added a 7 oz can of San Marcos Chilpotle Salsa and cooked on low for 1/2- 1 hour. I served it over rice. Excellent and not too salty. When the chicken is gone I will add a few pieces of skin on bone in thighs cook on low overnight then add black beans, corn,green chilies or bell pepper with chicken broth and make a soup as others have suggested. That is the good thing about chicken in crock pot, it is easy, foolproof and flexible.

I used 2 10 oz cans of rotel instead of salsa and cooked in my pressure cooker and it was amazing! Restaurant quality. (Ninja foodi) Coated the chicken in the mixture then removed the chicken, put mixture in the pot and place the chicken on the low rack and pressure cook on hi for 10 mins.

I make this quite often. I use low sodium taco seasoning and instead of salsa I use Rotel tomatoes with green chiles and you can buy them canned with no salt added. We eat it as tacos and then leftovers can become enchiladas.

My family loved this recipe! The only thing I did was I used more fresh lime juice . I used two limes and a cup of cilantro. The flavor was explosive! I used a fresh salsa. I cooked it on high for about 2 hours and then switched it to low. It was absolutely delicious!! This is a keeper! No need to fancy it up. I served it over Cilantro Lime Rice.. ( Rice a Roni) I added fresh lime juice to that and chopped fresh cilantro to add in after it was cooked. There wasn’t a drop left!!

I've made this several times. The first time it came out a bit too salty and I couldn't really taste the cilantro. Since then I use a lower sodium taco seasoning and I stir the fresh cilantro in at the very end so the flavor is nice and bright!
people, if the recipe is too salty try making your own taco seasoning without salt. recipes are meant to be modified to each persons taste.

I used the homemade taco seasoning mix (recipe on Allrecipes) as well as a good salsa. Was able to have chicken tacos as well as chicken tortilla soup out of this one batch! For the soup, I save about 1/3 of the cooked chicken and half of the remaining liquid, added 8oz of chicken broth, can of black beans and frozen corn. Added additional water (1-2 cups) and simmer till heated through. Topped it with cilantro, lime, cheese, and tortilla chips! (If I had any avocado would have been good too) My family loved both the tacos and the soup!

I have made this recipe 4 times in the past two weeks, and cant keep it in the fridge! I finally doubled it and am guarding it with my life!! It is so yummy and versatile! Definitely worth a try! I do add black beans, corn and green chilies to mine, so good!!!

This was easy and good. I did make my own salsa which probably helped. I made the taco seasoning from this site to cut back in salt a little. Cooked on high for 4 hours and it was perfect and easy to shred.

Wow! That says it all. Very easy to make and we had 2 great meals with this and still had some leftovers. We made enchiladas one night and tacos another. Outstanding flavor! I followed the recipe exactly with seasonings - BUT I used a whole chicken. It worked perfectly. I just didn't have 3 pounds of chicken breast. In the future, I'll make the whole chicken again. It was extremely economical! Started making this in 2012!
Sooooo good!!! I added a can of rotel, 3 sliced peppers, 1/2 onion, more cilantro, and a few tbsp of salsa…. Best thing since sliced bread!!! Making it again this week!

Added 1 can of black beans, 1 extra juiced lime, i bad of frozen corn and seasoned the chicken with paprika. Looks like it makes a ton of extra juice before you shred the chicken. After shredding, the juice is all soaked up. It's really good.

My family really liked this recipe. I used a store bought taco seasoning and the chickern was too salty. I will make my own taco seasoning next time and leave out the salt because the salsa already has salt. I will definitely make it again.

This was a delicious, easy dish. I intended to serve it as chicken tacos, but it was good enough to eat on its own. It also is a good lunch or dinner addition for anyone looking for lean protein while not sacrificing taste. I'll be making this again!
Made as stated and shredded with my hand mixer. Easy and good.
Made exactly as described and it was delicious - even better reheated. I threw on salads, tacos, rice and bean bowls...will definitely make again!
So easy and so, so good! Definitely will make again as there are so many ways to use delicious shredded chicken recipe. Thanks!
Super easy. I added lime zest to the crockpot and more fresh cilantro at the time we ate the tacos.
